Sarcoidosis: non-caseating granulomas; young adults; bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with or without parenchymal disease; erythema nodosum, arthralgia, uveitis, hypercalcaemia, raised ACE; Löfgren syndrome (bilateral hilar nodes + erythema nodosum + arthralgia, good prognosis).
Eye – uveitis, episcleritis: Extra‑intestinal sign, more common in Crohn’s.
Extra‑intestinal: primary sclerosing cholangitis, ankylosing spondylitis, uveitis, thromboembolic events, nutritional deficiencies (vit B12, iron, folate).

qs.q: A young adult under 40 years old presents with erythema nodosum, peripheral arthropathy, uveitis, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. What is the underlying pathophysiological mechanism of this multisystem disorder?
o: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to occupational organic dusts
Autoantibody production against type IV collagen in the membrane
Abnormal CD4 mediated cell reaction to an unknown antigen
Direct bacterial infection of the alveolar walls by tuberculosis
qs.e: Sarcoidosis is characterized by non-caseating granulomatous inflammation driven by an abnormal CD4-mediated cell reaction to an unknown antigen. It is not caused by active Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection despite forming granulomas.

qs.q: A 32-year-old man presents with erythema nodosum, peripheral arthropathy, uveitis, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Laboratory investigations reveal hypercalcemia. Which of the following is the underlying pathophysiological mechanism for the hypercalcemia in this multisystem granulomatous disorder?
o: Excessive dietary calcium absorption via altered gut mucosa
Increased formation of calcitriol by alveolar macrophages
Autoimmune destruction of the parathyroid gland receptors
Direct destruction of bony trabeculae by systemic granulomas
qs.e: Hypercalcemia in sarcoidosis occurs due to increased formation of calcitriol by the alveolar macrophages. It is not caused by direct bone destruction or parathyroid receptor autoimmunity.

qs.q: A 38-year-old man with sarcoidosis presents with severe uveitis and pulmonary impairment requiring systemic intervention. Which medication is specifically indicated to commence treatment for these manifestations?
qs.e: Prednisolone (20-40 mg/day) is commenced if pulmonary impairment, hypercalcemia, renal impairment, or uveitis are present. Azithromycin and diethylcarbamazine are not the primary systemic agents for sarcoidosis systemic management.
